items.title: Frank Netto Interview, 1986-11-10
items.q: Bill Padron stayed with us. He was with the band... the job expired and we decided that we could build Padron and myself.

ctx.x: We were at the Marigold and the guy was having problems with money.

Yeah, well, he liked to get an extra $75 to go to have his wife have his first child. And so we went up there and played an audition, I don't remember the fellow's name, but and he says how many, we played several tunes for him over there, Ain't She Sweet and those kind of tunes which was popular in those days, and the guy, and I was playing trumpet, and I went out there and the guy said how many tunes do you know? He says, I said well we can write down and we'll play 46 tunes for you. I didn't know we were at 46…
This was before the Owls recorded?

items.title: Frank Netto Interview, 1986-10-02
items.q: Bill and I were running the band at the time, Bill Padron.

ctx.x: I know the name. Yeah, he used to be an entertainer of some sort down there in the quarter. So he came down there with, sitting in a band, a rehearsal, and he'd come in there with a mustache and short pants. And I told him, I said, he sat down there and played and I said, well Ormond, I said one of them's got to go. Either short pants or got to go. So Bill and I were running the band at the time, Bill Padron. And we were splitting the liter price and that's how the argument wound up later. I said it don't make a…
I'm curious to ask, do you happen to remember a cornet player named Emmet Hardy?
